case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that when the division finds a report of abuse or neglect 'founded' and records that determination in the central registry it adjudicates the subject's status and must, under Part I, Article 15 of the State Constitution, give written notice of the determination, its reasons, the identification of the named perpetrator, and the rights of access and administrative challenge; the division's notice here was constitutionally inadequate.
key_cases.relevance: The court expressly grounds its analysis in the dangers of storing and using inaccurate government data about citizens, which is the constitutional frame for any automated cross-analysis of agency records.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the notification procedures employed by the division did not afford the Bagleys the protections required by part I, article 15 of the New Hampshire Constitution

key_cases.holding: In a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 action, the court held that state officials were not entitled to qualified immunity on the claim that listing the plaintiff in the central registry as a sex abuser without prior notice and hearing infringed a protected liberty interest, while immunity was properly claimed as to the asserted property interest in his private employment.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion identifies the permanent, cross-agency employment consequences of a single database entry, the key risk in any analysis of child welfare data systems.
key_cases.quote: we view Constantineau and Roth as requiring notice and hearing in advance of the listing, for the very reason that the listing effected a permanent disqualification from professional work

key_cases.case_name: Union Leader Corp. v. N.H. Dep't of Safety
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the dismissal of a Right-to-Know suit for State Police records of the response to the Sununu Youth Services Center, clarifying that juvenile confidentiality under RSA 169-B:35 reaches records held by non-court agencies only to the extent disclosure would run counter to the purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors, and remanded for that determination and for consideration of redaction.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion sets the disclosure boundary for any public dataset built on New Hampshire juvenile and youth-facility records.
key_cases.quote: This refinement effectuates the juvenile delinquency statutes’ purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors while also ensuring “the greatest possible public access to the actions, discussions and records of all public bodies.”
